landing.pitch: An editor for interactive narrative works that speaks the grammar of cinema. Write in Shots, cut between Scenes, and hand a Reader one link.
landing.signInFailed: Signing in did not work. Please try again.
landing.specimenShot: The door gives on the third push. Rain, and the neon of the bar opposite, already lit at four in the afternoon.
landing.specimenCutTwo: Stay in the doorway until it eases
landing.made: What a Story is made of

terms.storyLine: A whole work, owned by you and handed to a Reader as one link.
terms.sceneLine: A linear run of Shots, and the only unit at which a Story branches.
terms.shotLine: One beat: an image, its text, or both. The smallest thing a Reader is shown.
terms.cutLine: A way on from one Scene to another, offered at the end of a Scene for the Reader to take.
terms.conditionLine: A test that decides whether a Shot plays or a Cut is offered, so the same Scene reads differently without ever branching.

landing.reading: Read a published Story on the engine a Reader runs

cue.heading: Next
cue.dismiss: I can take it from here
cue.nameScene: Every Story starts with a Scene. Name one here — “The arrival” will do — and it lands on the bench ready for its first Shot.
cue.openScene: A Scene is folded on the graph until you open it. Open this one, and what is inside is the run of Shots a Reader plays.
cue.writeShot: A Shot is a Still and its text, as much as the Reader is shown at once. Add one, and write the first thing they read.
cue.secondScene: A Story branches between Scenes, never inside one. Name a second Scene here, the one this Scene leads to.
cue.drawCut: A Cut is the way on. Drag from the strip down the edge of the first Scene onto the second, and let go.
cue.setFlag: State is what one Reading carries with it. Give this Scene a Flag — “courage = high” — and it is set on every Reader who enters.
cue.openingScene: A Reading has to start somewhere, and nothing marks where this Story does. Open a Scene and mark it as the one to start on — any of them will do, and you can name another whenever you like.
cue.putCondition: A Condition makes the same Scene play differently to different Readers, without branching. Open the second Scene, add a Shot, and have it played when that Flag holds something else — “low” will do. Nothing plays it yet, which is the point.
cue.previewCondition: Nothing plays that Shot, and the Preview says why: it reads the Story on the engine a Reader runs, and shows what each Shot it skipped asked for beside what the State actually holds. Open it, read that, then come back and put the value right.
cue.publish: That is a Story that works. Publish it, and anybody can read it at a link of its own — the one this page then shows, to hand to whoever you wrote it for.
